en: I bow to Vaidyanātha,
whose deep navel is like the lotus-born Brahmā’s, and who serves as the abode for the play of his divine manifestations.
O wise ones, for the purification of knowledge,
take refuge in Vaidyanātha, who stands at the forefront of the learned;
and in the generals of the rat-vehicled deity (Gaṇeśa), Pārvatī, and the Supreme Lord (Śiva).

For the perpetual attainment of all auspiciousness, I perpetually prostrate myself. Now, in the *Yajurveda*, regarding the letter *a* at the end of words occurring in the fifty *pratipada*s and so forth; the letter *na* at the end of words; the *pragraha* status of the word-final letter *ta*; the letters *i* and *u* at the beginning of words; the *saṃhitā* and *avasāna* [endings]; the *ṣatva* and *ṇatva* changes of the *Saṃhitā*; the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) vowels *e* and *o* at the beginning of subsequent words; the word-final letter *ṅa*; the three long vowels resulting from the lengthening of similar syllables at the end of words; and that which indicates even or odd numbers and expresses the number of *visarga*s—for each of these fifty [categories], there is one syllable per *anuvāka* and one sentence per [category].

We shall now explain the Jewel of Characteristics (*lakṣaṇaratna*). Here, the consonants that initiate [the phonemes] are the vowels beginning with *a* and ending with *u*, excluding the protracted (*pluta*) vowels—these are five. There are also five vowels beginning with *ū* and ending with *o*, excluding *ṛ* and *ḷ*. The consonants are: *ka-ga*, *ca-ja*, *ṭa-ḍa*, *ta-da*, *pa-ba*, *ma-na*, *la-va*, and *śa-sa*.

In this context, having combined the respective pairs of examples joined by *dvandva* compounds and disregarding their singular nature, one should observe whether the number [of syllables] is even or odd: the letter *a* placed at the beginning of a word and the letter *n* at the end of a word are even in the case of two *ka*s, and odd in the case of two *ca*s; the letter *ta* at the end of a word and the *pragraha* (svarabhakti) are even in the case of two *ṭa*s, and odd in the case of two *ta*s; the letter *iṃ* and the letter *ya* at the beginning of a word are even in the case of two *la*s, and odd in the case of two *ma*s; and all three of these pairs of examples are even in the case of two *la*s, and odd in the case of two *śa*s.

It should be understood that where one pair of *lakṣyas* is either even or odd, the other pair of *lakṣyas* therein shall be the opposite. Among the eight pairs, the first and last syllables respectively indicate the even and odd numbers of the *saṃhitā* and *avasāna*. In the case of the eight pairs, when there is a conjunction of *yakāra* and *vakāra* with any other consonant, an irregularity (*vaiṣamya*) regarding the *ṣatva* and *ṇatva* rules of *saṃhitā* should be observed; in the absence of such a conjunction, it should be understood that they are indeed even (*sama*).

In the case of the combination of the letter *r* with two sets of eight [consonants], a single substitute (*ekādeśa*) should be observed as irregular (*vaiṣamya*) when it occurs before the initial vowels *e* or *o* of a following word, or at the end of a word, or before the consonant *ṅ*. It should be understood that in the absence of such a combination, it is regular (*sama*). Furthermore, the three long vowels resulting from the coalescence of identical syllables at the end of a word are regular within the first group of five vowels, but irregular within the second group of five vowels.

Having divided the five groups of *visarjanīya*s into sets of five, within the final group of five, the number of *visarjanīya*s should be understood as one, two, three, four, and five, respectively, by means of the vowels beginning with *a* and those beginning with *ū*. Here, the *mapara-svara* (the vowel following *m*) indicates the absence of the *visarjanīya*. In this context, the indivisible particle *māṅ* is not to be considered as a word-final (*padalakṣya*). Thus, terminal prefixes (*upasarga*s) are not to be counted among word-final elements. A *pragraha* (protracted vowel) is not to be counted in the enumerations of long vowels.
"The absence of a [word-final] element shall be equal"—thus ends the *Lakṣaṇaratnaparibhāṣā* composed by Vaidyanātha Bhaṭṭa.

Oṃ, for strength, thee! Mā | pyuśo | ṭu | caṭyo | lyau śe | cya | liso | śya | me ca śe | cvīcyūku | myecū | bū | jūmailvī | vyośalaikyū | āpadaṃdantu | ṭaupyā | ṭaṭapo | bubālīka | ṭiṭī | cīlū | bye | ṭyai | bālu | la | lutū | ṭauṭvi | leśoci | pyecīsā | nesipyātaibvipuṭyo devasya tvā | kyāto | kyaiṭo | te | topvicu | mvī | lyacai | loji | pyamau | kicā | cryukā | kutu | ḍī | jūjā | byevyūnokiśutoḍāpu.

I take [thee]. Thou art the pressing-stone (*grāvan*). *Cyubyau*. *Cyupau pekulailīpaujyulyūtvī*. Taken with the *upayāma* vessel. *Pītuṭaupucālomyāmyūceli*. Never (*kadācana*). *Laive*. *Lūcyau cepakicīṭīpī*. The deliverer (*taraṇiḥ*). *Kyavuḍyaityepoṭhama*. Ascend (*ātiṣṭha*). *Pījucūmyumākī*. *Kaucai*. *Dyaibucū*. *Ḍaiseja*. *Śekūṭā*. Om.

The gods and the asuras; the Maumācitashas; the Mautakākemaus; the Lyuṭālas; the Tityatepamūs; the Kovaujusaus; the Ṭyodeśūśūnus; the Kekaipīśamailis; the Macitītaumilus; the Meśikatūśulumpres; the Jūgainīcus; the Saśaimaibvīmyos—Oṃ, I sprinkle you. The Ḍaṭāṭas; the Kījāṭyus; the Culpūs; the Śaiśotāṭas; the Tāṭiṭvīs; the Dusai-bives; the Lipūlukīcyutepūs; the Pyūcūlelas; the Ṭaṭimapeteṭos; the Caśocacalemilvīs; the Vyāsyākīcyaitādes.

Oṃ! To Pākayajña indeed! To Tomī-śūti-tilū! To Tyūmya-upāmi! To Śūko-mīlu! To Lyokya-tekya-śate! To Lūpya-imaśya! To Limā-kūpya-eśakauṭau! To Nāku! To Latā-śaine! To Jyotā! To Buṭaiḍe! To Śyoma-u! To Cumyo! To Syāpautya-ṭyai-śyai! Oṃ! To Anumati, the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa)! To Lvīlau! To Carma! To Śai! To Gaunā! To Vyaisobai! To Tuḍo! To Tīmo! To Cyo! To Cvriṭaku! To Ṭīcutī! To Myū! To Lidāṭī! To Ṭainigi! To Cīso! To Māsryū! To Cesē! To Lyi! To Mu! To Mrai! To Tī! To Vre! To Vu! To Kābonīcyusaugo!

Oṃ vāyavyaṃ śvetam | pākyuṭyelatāte | paiśatakūlau tilviśauṭe | cokau ṭrilviṭvī | tetaṭotyumryecūlaucī | tricyaucviśopātaśi | ṭaimitolūśau | caiṭaiśaśupeśāpī | pilūpatāti | ṭuṭaikūcā | śuśūśa | gaulujaiṭetuṭo.

Oṃ! Prajāpati [created] the creatures. Ṭetaimaimicye | Tūtyāṭaśīlā | Pīkaucaṭau | Lalyaukacaṭepauṭiḍū | Ṭaipulipomulaica | Ṭekakīmaicī | Pīlaulaleka | Śāpyūmīśemrutru | Kaikucyālelūmaimo | Tāśaipauluśyau | Śācumāśaṭīśi | Cesījyausainyuṭībobyo.

Oṃ! To the Ādityas, those who abide in the world; mu-ṭai-mū-śe-ṭau; lā-śakī-śeka-uśryoti-kokyū; kv-rī-kre-pyā-le-mau; ce-ṭyu-lucū; pri-mra-pai; ṭā-talā; pū-śumā-ko; kvī-śī-pai; kī-pai-ṭī; śyā-mvi-motū; cyā-lvī-pyaucyukū; mai-tā; lyopū-ṭvi-ṭu;

ḍvīti-śāṭya-ṭvi-de. Oṃ! Gods and humans; cā-mukye-krya; śacī-mupī; mo-macā; pa-kicu; lau-gi; ci-lu; ca-gī; je-pu; cai-mi-caimī; ṭe-ṭra-pū; lyakā-kopemyukau; kyāl-vrī-ṭitā-pitū-lu; mru; bo-pumū-ṭyelvi.

Oṃ, Viśvarūpa indeed. Crilomuṭumyūlame. Kūmrailyākūṭāpyūṭyau. Ślūśūcaipemīlailau. Mīcatoṭyomai. Celuśaupāpāmrī. Śūpaupoṭracuśe. Śalvimoṭaimvī. Tīṭvīpīlākaiṭyaucu. Lyuṭimīkūṭaile. Cvīṭyāpicau. Tiṭoṭūkekakemyopepā. Nākotūḍīḍvī.

*Oṃ*. He sacrifices the fuel-sticks (*samidh*). Piṭi-pyā-picilo-śī | Ṭaic-yuṭy-emūtyo-pe | Ṭuṭī-cā-kataik-vī | Capā-cailu | Śro-cvītyota-tīmai | Śilu-lyaute-tapau | Myām-raupyo-culū-śyū | Co-śau-śom-vī-śu-śaupi | Trai-pā-śū-pauta-lelī | Śau-ṭū-mvī-cī | Vya-aildyuta | Byo-ṭāl-vi-pvilaj-vī.
*Oṃ*. Prajāpati desired. Līmā-caula | Peca-meṭau | Comā-ṭī | Cye-ṭelyela-u | Pikā | Śijvi-śau | Pī-śa-śāk-yu | Ṭyu-bucu | Nonicu-sailu-śū | Ṭaipyū-vya | Kātau-vyonyuletyasryaitai.
Oṃ. He who indeed [is] among the *pavamāna*s; ṭāśaupyā sausyaito; *lyaliḍuṭau*; ḍetitaimyolū; maucaikrakamābeja; ḍogyāṭyu; cakamī; cyelosūśekevā; pyālaumvilīluśyūkrau; tyutau; śvībokī. Oṃ.
O Agni, full of splendor! kicu; mauce; pāḍibilau; maupyaimi; ṭaiśyucuṭelo; mācāśu; cakutī; kilūjipuṭaicū; ḍūḍī; ḍūvyū; kvīsaunyaityomyū.

Oṃ vivā etasya | pauśumātvi | lyaḍvī | cvīśvilyutīmāmaṭo | ṭiki | sau | śucai | cyotojā | śutīpuculyalapu | lūkyauśaucutūlyauśyai | tyumaṭītyopai | jujīṭaubīgaibvi | Oṃ pūrṇāpaścāt | josryepūkuśī | śocyūcelyū ca | ṭauto | caulūsīto | dumojyau | tyāpānyo | komipā | śyau | kumotī | vyācaumyu | śyocyūmvikrāḍu.

Oṃ *yuñjānaḥ prathamam*. Naigaḍaudyau. Kagatīdauḍu. Butraulīḍya. Kyośyaugāḍye. Mibyakūścī. Ṭyūpūcyū. Kūpiḍopai. Pokabyesukede. Ḍovāvū. Ṭudolukaśai. Ḍīganutu. Oṃ *viṣṇoḥ kramosi*. Ṭaiṭyūmailanyau. Najucādi. Nyobvimāgo. Ṭījībyemā. Tipinyedamyaṭu. Devausyāśevī. Mākinyuḍyai. Bevyaino. Cuśīḍocūkepau. Vyelaupīga. Mūvaugvi.

Oṃ apāntveman | cya | kopatī | ṭuṭviṭau | baucviṭe | myumyo | śedvī | jvicū | pye | pyuki | līśamau | butālejvībyo | śyenaṭvi | bīdocaitigyaśyasyauko | Oṃ, you are a ray of light | myācyolye | lalokye | popīkūpopā | pyepimanecaipaiḍryāḍi | laṭau | tulaśu | lauṭu | te | śū | māśutu | tośopāmo | nyālaiśidamyā |
Oṃ, obeisance to you, O Rudra! To the one who is satisfied and pure! Mīmū! Śūko! Pelī! Cyalu! Cucu! Maulū! Muśa! Lulā! Vyākyobiḍoṭo! Nāḍā!
Oṃ, they have come for strength! Ḍadūnvinībā! Gyaubājūpyaivyeba! Śosyaṭacauvai! Śikūjūśuṭe! Jyājūmvīṭuvodū! Nvīcūgyabavubyaikyau! Ḍyūdūdāvyūḍi! Dryāluduni! Byagucyaino!

*Oṃ agnāviṣṇū | śvimo | mauke | ṭucau | kotu | cīca | cimi | cāma | mi | lyai | śakyai | mote | śīpaitu | noṭvidukipi | jojyesyako | hyeśaumauvatebyugvī | Oṃ, he offers the Sāvitrī oblations: kvīṭikaumaupa | lyupāpauṭitokvī | laukrailūcyakai | cyoṭiṭauputūce | kyalaṭyośautotamupyocvīlu | pomātaupī | tyeṭapāpya | pyaimācyaupoṭrikaka | lūcyauśvīkomukya | śūcaipauśyacye | gyulvipekau.*

Oṃ, they are indeed headed by Viṣṇu. Myai-muti-śyucu-meśa. Śamya-śatai-śūlī. Ṭau-ṭalī-tuci-myutu. Mātau-ṭaśvī. Tū-śācyai-śāṭo-śamā. Cī-leli-taic-yu. Muṭyai-kyai-mic-vī. Pyā-ṭyū-kyo-po-ko-palū-śyū. Me-ṭyu-śyo-lī-ṭyutu. Lū-cī-te-kyai-mye-kvi-śu. Pe-nai. Jo-pi. Oṃ, the sacrifice has been destroyed. Kī-ṭā-śili-tū. Lī-kā-śī-kyūm-vī. Pai-poly-o-mai-kau. Lu-śyai-tūt-vikī-śecu. Mai-kyā-ṭaly-aṭya. Lyai-māty-au. Kai-pyū-cyuc-vī. Ci-śapy-au. Ṭī-tyā. Kū-mite-kau. Kā-kvī-lālī. Po-ṭau.
Oṃ! Devāsuraḥ | Pūṭecāk | Maukyācocca | Śimākrāketi | Cyaipvīlūpaśye | Cecimyapūṭvī | ŚutaImokīkyuśau | Ṭoṭemyauśauṭecakyu | Cviṭyāṭaitīkauli | Ṭyāṭyotopai | Tyaśaupyaupama | Ciṭākaimi | Kyuṭikye.

Oṃ yadekena | crulracaucupīpīpau | mīmaiśapuśuṭiku | tīprīkyū | mometaili | ṭupepyaipyai | piśumau | pātyāmaukūmyai | mryāśucye | pātyaikyāmīcau | ṭāliśītomuṭicu | indrāyarājñe | micoṭucacūpālalulekīcūṭamaimu | Oṃ hiraṇyavarṇāśśucayaḥ | bopyecunū | śamyalokeśailā | cātuṭyālā | letaipvīkaila | kupaumū | lutiśriṭau | pūṭatoṭai | tyūṭyāpyūlaipicvi | śyaipośā | tūkautyā | licumilimrīloṭilaiṭecūmimucī ||

Oṃ yovā ayathā devatam | Śyaitauśa | Jyākāgyaimabauśa | Śaikīcocī | Laiṭauṭiśau | Tācīkopupecopro | Ṭrakauśecutyaike | Gūpaiśau | Pitalū | Latūpūtyaimū | Trīpyauṭu | Kośuṭūcyaulūlrīluṭaimoṭhacīṭūlelaisāṭyeko.

Oṃ, he constructs the hall with its beams directed toward the east: *ṭela-śaukyo-ṭocopilyūkū*, *lyalī-paul-e-caṭaiśa*, *tota-mūṭolī-śīpāpa*, *makvi-ṭākaut-vilupacaiṭu*, *kvimi-kyumāmro*, *śaumimai-ṭailyoteṭai*, *mumīlākai-śviṭolāśu*, *puśimolakā*, *kyauśre-pūkakauṭekya*, *ce-cītyepyūmi*, *kāmīpucyeka-utyecai*.

Oṃ! Having released both: *ṭyu-śo-tyete-kaucyū-pī*, *śaikyām-vī-micikī-ki*, *kośv-auśryā-cviṭī*, *kemra-mā-ṭa-śo-ta*, *ṭa-śeka-iṭū-lau*, *pūtū-taul-yū*, *pepa-iko-ṭepyu*, *keṭy-auṭyuke-mīmā*, *pyapu-śī-picū*, *cucau-śreṭū-mokai-śri*, *pyeśv-ipvipū*.

Oṃ. From the *cātvāla* [pit]: śe-śi-ṭī-prī-ṭrī-śryā; cya-ipyo-śau-maluce; mi-lu-pol-yautrā-kau; crū-kai-makū-kvī-lī-maic-au-pvī; kau-ṭi-ṭau-śai; ca-pam-ī-me; lī-tā-ṭau-lvī-lvī; pi-mau-ṭry-ātī; co-cālā-śe-ṭyau-kā; cya-aut-au-lvī-śyai-kyu-śau;

kī-mau-ṭo-ṭik-yaum-vi. Oṃ. By means of the sacrifice (*yajña*), indeed: kyu-śā-to-lyai-mū; me-le-pu-śyau-lyā-lo-ṭa; lo-pyai-ma-ṭik-ya; lo-pū-ṭyau-kvī; ṭri-le-cī-co-pau-lyek-vī; ṭi-lok-yā-ka; cai-śyai-pvi-pū; me-śo-mo; t-yu-lo-cau-śya-ṭyu; ṭai-ṭya-tau-lām-ā-śe; to-kip-ailu.

Oṃ! Indra for Vṛtra; Kāpaṭekaiśā; Tīcrikī; Taiceśyālu; Pipri; Lāpetūpe; Kukaicicākapo; Tutyocyau; Ṭvipauloṭaukomā; Caumaimaśyo; Līkyepo; Crītityaumi. Oṃ! For the heavenly world indeed; Lyacaumūmaipu; Tyāśucai; Ṭyupyaulomotai; Tūṭaupipīcicū; Lucrelepo; Māko; Ṭībaicopi; Tipyecote; Laipyai; Śākyau; Cāśeśaipaumāke.

Oṃ, the light of procreation! Lumaukvicautyūmūkya! Ṭyapyāpu! Lyaikīmvī! Līkaucyopyūṭośāśā! Latecaipucamyāvudyamo! Laukakūśvi! Lemū! Kī! Śuṭaṭumā! Lutī! Lvi! Myam! Lom! Kau! Lom! Mū! Luvyā! Ṭyom mom kom kū! Śī!

Om. The gods are indeed to be accomplished. Tātyekracau. Śyācyūkī. Śālyai. Lośośe. Teśrututūpailyū. Lepemyu. Ṭvimyācūmeṭyeṭyu. Cepokipūcruṭuśau. Cyūciścī. Pāpyokakā. Ekasmai. Kātīcītaicyulaiṭūcam cuśū. Om. By this, indeed, one moves with speed. Cālitate. Maupom. Tucau. Pīpi. Śelipryailū. Crīśī. Pyaiṭulotryū. Śīcā. Śaṭitryī. Śāśyeṭāṭūṭo. Ṭryumuḍai. Kyo. Dvi. Kya. Lū. Śāmī. Cam. Com. La. Lai.

Oṃ! Bṛhaspati desired: *mikito*, *mauśūcotiṭrai*, *mitūpalimyeśū*, *ṭipūkvrī*, *lrau lyo cutu*, *cāṭiśi*, *kyāśyucī*, *kotaicā*, *kū*, *cyaipai*, *ṭvipyailīke*, *lu*, *lu*, *tī*, *mūlā*, *dejyu*, *tesu*, *śābīśūtu*, *ligau*, *mvi*, *lom*.

*Oṃ*. These are indeed the [syllables]: *pyauṭāśyācātalye*, *śītī*, *śākya*, *lākī*, *ṭyapū*, *mūlyūtaitā*, *loṭūpijo*, *śicyaulyakaityā*, *tācocepī*, *lā*, *lam śau*, *śauṃ mi*, *kvi*, *ce*, *lyāṭāśi*, *śai*, *ṭau*, *lyu*, *cemyu*, *ke*, *ta*, *śā*, *ṭoṭu*, *mi*, *śyomu*.
Thus ends the *Lakṣaṇaratna*, composed by the venerable Vaidyanātha Bhaṭṭa, who is esteemed by the learned knowers of the Vedas.
